provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Out family batch. Small, high-margin niche that sells at night: the kit leans on night demos, techniques and service plans. Standard direction is C48, not C39 (night photography). No fixture or transformer brands named. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Uplighting, moonlighting from trees, path and step lights, wall washing, grazing stone, silhouetting, and where glare comes from
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers don't know what they want until they see the names and the effects. A technique page gives them words to ask for.

pageStructurePlus.contains: What happens at a night demo, temporary fixtures on the house and trees, adjusting angles live, and how the demo fee credits toward the install
pageStructurePlus.why: Lighting sells after dark. The demo is how most installs close, so booking it is the site's real job.

pageStructurePlus.contains: LED low-voltage fixtures, transformer sizing, buried wire runs, photocells, astronomical timers, zones and phone control
pageStructurePlus.why: Owners have seen cheap solar stakes fail. Explaining the system shows why a professional install lasts.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Annual night check, re-aiming fixtures as plants grow, cleaning lenses, repairing wire cut by aerators, and holiday lighting tie-ins
pageStructurePlus.why: Lighting needs adjusting as gardens grow. A service plan page turns every install into recurring work.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Lighting columns, stone walls, entries and signage on homes, churches, restaurants and office fronts, with dark-sky friendly fixtures
pageStructurePlus.why: Facade work brings commercial buyers who search differently and spend more. A separate page catches them.

designDirections.name: Book a Night Demo
designDirections.bestFor: Small lighting outfits that win by getting a night demo booked fast
designDirections.headlineSample: Outdoor lighting design and install in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's combo on a lean page: linen keeps daytime text easy to read, and brick red makes the night demo button unmissable.

designDirections.name: After Dark
designDirections.bestFor: Lighting designers whose whole portfolio is night photography of lit homes and gardens
designDirections.headlineSample: Homes and gardens lit beautifully in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Not the family combo because this work is shown at night: a near-black ground lets lit facades glow instead of looking washed out on linen, and Didone headings feel gallery-grade.

designDirections.name: Brass at Dusk
designDirections.bestFor: Architectural lighting firms working on estates, churches and commercial facades
designDirections.headlineSample: Architectural lighting for {City} estates and facades
designDirections.whyItFits: Navy and brass echo solid-brass fixtures at dusk, and the editorial serif suits buyers who compare lighting designers, not installers.

openers.line: Your lighting work is some of the best night photography I've seen from a local outfit, and your listing has no site to show it. People pick a lighting designer by looking at lit houses.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Where those lit houses could live: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing links to Facebook, where your best uplit facade is compressed into a tiny thumbnail. Night lighting needs a dark, full-screen page to look the way it does in person.
openers.hook: Tap the link and confirm it goes to Facebook. Note their best night shot there.
openers.linkLine: Your outdoor lighting on a dark, full-screen page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your site shows fixtures in daylight, brass stakes in mulch, but hardly any lit homes at night. Buyers buy the glow, not the fixture.
openers.hook: Open their site and count night versus daytime shots. If daytime dominates, use this.
openers.linkLine: A lighting site built around the night view: {demo-link}

openers.line: On a phone your lighting gallery loads so dark and compressed the facades turn to grey blobs. Most people see your work on a phone, at night, in bed.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on a phone in a dim room and note what fails. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your night lighting, crisp on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to book a night lighting demo without calling during the day. Buyers think about lighting at night, standing in a dark driveway.
openers.hook: Check listing, bios and any site for a demo or consult form. If none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A night demo request that works after dark: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Night shots buried in the feed
openers.line: The moonlit oak and the grazed stone chimney on your Instagram are portfolio pieces. In the feed they sit between daytime install posts and disappear.
openers.hook: Find two strong night shots and name the technique: moonlighting, grazing, path lights. Mention one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your lighting work, sorted by technique: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews talk about pulling into the driveway and loving the house again, and steps that are finally safe at night. That's the feeling a lighting buyer wants, and it stays on your listing.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about the look or safety. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the lit homes they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: When the clocks change and it's dark by dinner, people notice their house disappears at night. That's the month outdoor lighting gets searched.
openers.hook: Use in September and October, before the clock change. Mention the date in the reply.

openers.line: Lighting buyers browse at night by definition, often after a party where the yard was dark. A demo request form catches them while the thought is fresh.
openers.hook: Call the listed number after hours. A generic or full voicemail means the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A lighting demo request that works at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring a lighting tech. Good low-voltage installers look at the quality of a company's lit homes before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the role and date.
openers.linkLine: A lighting company site with a careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your lighting jobs cluster in a few neighbourhoods, but nothing tells someone in {Neighborhood} you light homes there. 'Landscape lighting' plus the town is the search.
openers.hook: Find towns or neighbourhoods tagged on their posts; use the most upscale one they name.
openers.linkLine: A lighting page for each neighbourhood you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you let clients light the front first and the backyard next season, say so on the site. Lighting sold in phases is easier to say yes to.
openers.hook: Only if they mention phasing or financing publicly. Otherwise skip.

openers.line: Lighting buyers worry about cheap fixtures corroding and wires cut in the lawn. Your insurance, fixture warranty and service promise on one page answers that.
openers.hook: Look for any mention of warranty or insurance. Note what's there; never invent terms.
openers.linkLine: Fixture warranty and service, stated plainly: {demo-link}

openers.angle: The lit house on the street
openers.line: A beautifully lit house is the one the whole street notices on the walk home. Those neighbours still look up the lighting company before they call.
openers.hook: Look for comments or reviews mentioning neighbours. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where the next lighting referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you lit is beautiful, especially the way the trees are moonlit. That should be the first night shot a stranger sees.
openers.hook: Pick their newest night shot and name the house style and techniques used.
openers.linkLine: That lighting job, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} is gorgeous lighting work. The moonlit trees especially.

I was looking for outdoor lighting companies in {City} and found {Business Name} on Instagram, but no site where someone can see your night work full screen and book a night demo. I built a sample lighting site to show the idea, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case this got buried. Here's the sample lighting site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It's built dark so night work glows, sorts jobs by technique, and has a night demo request form. If it's not for you, say so and I'll leave it.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for outdoor lighting companies in {City}. I sent you a note about a sample site. Did you catch it?"

IF NO:
"No problem. It's a sample lighting site for {Business Name}, dark background so night shots glow, a techniques page and a night demo request, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, then ask how many demos they run a month
"It runs {Build Range} depending on how many technique and neighbourhood pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For your company I'd quote about {Build Price}, less than one front-of-house lighting package."
"Can we look at it together for ten minutes this week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a short scope and deposit invoice. It's live before the clocks change."

objections.objection: My work comes from landscapers and builders.
objections.handler: "Those partners are great. Their clients still look you up before the demo, and a site full of lit homes makes your number feel reasonable."

objections.objection: Night shots are hard to get.
objections.handler: "That's why the site starts with marked placeholders. We swap in night shots as you get them, and I can arrange a dusk shoot when you're ready."
"Great. Happy to hand over the dark gallery layout and the demo form. If it stalls before autumn, the offer stands."

objections.objection: People think solar stakes from the hardware store are the same thing.
objections.handler: "The systems page explains transformers, wire and real fixtures in plain words. It's the answer you give on every demo, written once."

objections.objection: It's summer, nobody's thinking about lighting.
objections.handler: "That's why now. The site is built and found by the time the evenings get dark and the searches start."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}: a night gallery, a techniques page, a demo request and neighbourhood pages. Less than lighting one front walk."

email.subject: Lighting site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for outdoor lighting companies in {City} and made a sample one for {Business Name}. I'll text the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm switching off the {Business Name} lighting demo on Friday.

Keep it on for you? Yes or no is fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, the evenings are getting shorter and outdoor lighting searches pick up with them. Thought of you.

The sample lighting site is still up, same price: {demo-link}

bullets: Price the gallery by night shots, not pages; a lighting site lives or dies on how the lit homes look.
The night demo request is the conversion point. Price it as its own line with scheduling built in.
Peg the build to one front-of-house lighting package, never to hours.
Charge for the facade lighting page only when the company does commercial or architectural work.
Sell the service plan page as part of every build; it turns installs into recurring visits.
Budget extra time for image tuning; dark photos need careful compression to look right on phones.

lineItems.item: Night gallery tuned for dark backgrounds
lineItems.description: Max with day and night pairs, technique filters and careful compression for phones.

lineItems.item: Night demo request with evening scheduling
lineItems.description: Max with sunset-aware time slots, a demo fee option and areas-of-interest checkboxes.
Max with a short explainer, a diagram and three night examples of the technique.
Max with plan tiers, an online sign-up and a past-customer lookup.
Max with commercial references, dark-sky notes and a bid request form.
Max when each page shows lit homes from that neighbourhood.

whatElseYouSell.name: Blue-hour lighting photo shoot
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One evening at your best lit home, shot in the twenty minutes after sunset when the sky is still blue. Those are the shots that sell outdoor lighting."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, on the next install the owners are proud of.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts of lit homes
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A home with your lighting on goes onto your Maps profile each week with the neighbourhood named, so the listing glows next to competitors' daytime stakes."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review asks the night after install
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The evening after install, when the timer first switches the lights on, the homeowner gets a text asking for a review."

whatElseYouSell.name: Clock-change lighting campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A campaign that starts the week the clocks fall back, when every homeowner notices their house going dark at dinner."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in August, run late October through November.

whatElseYouSell.name: Holiday lighting add-on pages
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "If you also hang holiday lights, a seasonal page sells it to your landscape lighting customers first."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, ahead of the holidays, only if they offer it.

whatElseYouSell.name: Night lighting tour for prospects
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short evening drive past three homes with your lighting, with past clients' permission, booked through the site. Prospects see the real glow."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 4, in autumn, with willing past clients.

whatElseYouSell.name: Lighting lookbook for builders and designers
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A printed and online lookbook of your lit homes for the builders and landscape designers who get asked 'who did the lights'."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the gallery is full.

withoutAI.whoPays: The landscape design firm, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The garden designers whose beds you light need sites that show the gardens at night as well as by day. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Designers and lighting installers share projects; night views make the designer's site better too.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The supply house where you buy fixtures and wire has a showroom no homeowner can find online. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Supply houses have budgets and an installer list that is your prospect list.

withoutAI.whoPays: The holiday lighting company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The holiday light crew in your area works the same houses every December. Their site can send year-round lighting work to you."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Seasonal and permanent lighting share buyers and swap referrals.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The builder whose homes you light needs a portfolio site with dusk shots, and you already have them."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Builders love dusk photography of their homes; the lighting client provides it.

withoutAI.whoPays: The pool or hardscape builder, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Every pool and outdoor kitchen you light at night is the builder's best photo. Their site needs it as much as yours."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same backyard, same buyer, and the lighting makes their work look its best.

withoutAI.route: Churches and restaurants with dark facades
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The church whose steeple you lit needs a site for services and events, and it's easier to say yes to the person who made the building glow."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Commercial lighting clients already trust the installer, and many have weak sites.

withAI.route: Fixture and wire calculator for the supply house
withAI.pitchLine: "Installers enter the fixtures and run lengths and the assistant sizes the transformer and wire gauge, priced from that supply house."
withAI.whyItWorks: It ties installers to one supplier and cuts sizing mistakes.

withAI.route: Night view preview for landscape designers
withAI.pitchLine: "Designers upload a daytime garden and get a clearly labelled night preview with suggested lighting, to sell the lighting add-on."
withAI.whyItWorks: Designers sell more lighting, and the lighting client installs it.

withAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners describe the roofline and trees and the assistant drafts a holiday lighting quote, flagging year-round lighting interest."
withAI.whyItWorks: Holiday crews are slammed in autumn; leads flagged for permanent lighting go to your client.

withAI.route: Event and service assistant for churches
withAI.pitchLine: "Visitors ask service times and parking at night. An assistant answers from the church calendar, including the lit evening events."
withAI.whyItWorks: Small offices need after-hours help; the lighting client made the introduction.

withAI.pitchLine: "The builder logs each finished home and the assistant schedules a blue-hour lighting shoot with sunset times and the homeowner's okay."
withAI.whyItWorks: Builders want dusk shots of every home; the lighting client gets credit on each.

withAI.route: HOA entrance and amenity lighting tracker
withAI.pitchLine: "Residents report dark entrance signs and burned-out path lights with a picture; the assistant logs them and sends repairs to one lighting company."
withAI.whyItWorks: Dark common areas are a safety complaint; the lighting client gets the repair queue.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for lighting enquiries
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Calls you miss during an evening demo get a text asking new lighting, a repair, or adding to an existing system, plus the address."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and approved wording.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for lighting installs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each review gets a reply drafted that mentions the lit trees or the safer steps, ready for you to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Night demo scheduler with sunset times
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Demo slots move with sunset through the year, so a homeowner books a lighting demo that actually happens in the dark."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their demo length, crew availability and service area.

softwareAI.name: Deposit and install billing for lighting jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Demo fee at booking, deposit at signing, balance the night the lights are aimed, each sent with a card link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their fee and deposit rules and payment account.

softwareAI.name: Lighting package price guide
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners pick front facade, trees, path and backyard and see a fixture-count range before the demo, so nobody's surprised after dark."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their per-fixture pricing and typical package sizes.

softwareAI.name: Night lighting preview from a daytime picture
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner uploads a daytime picture of the house and sees a clearly labelled night preview with uplights and path lights, before booking the demo."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a set of their day and night pairs to tune against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Service plan renewal and night-check reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every lighting client gets a yearly night check reminder and a plan renewal. That's steady service work from installs you already did."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs past installs with dates and their service plan price.

softwareAI.name: Lighting chatbot on techniques, fixtures and timers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'what's moonlighting' and 'can I control the lights from my phone' at night, from your own notes, and books the demo."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their technique and system notes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: System map per property
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each lit property gets a map of fixtures, wire runs, transformer and zones, so service calls start with the layout instead of a guess."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their install notes and a simple sketch per job.

softwareAI.name: After-hours lighting enquiry line
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Evening callers get answered: what they want lit, rough size of the property, and a night demo booked on your calendar."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their calendar and screening questions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Transformer and wire sizing tool
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter the fixtures and run lengths, and the tech gets transformer size, wire gauge and voltage drop before the truck leaves."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their fixture wattages and wiring rules.

softwareAI.name: Client portal with design approval and service history
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Clients approve the lighting plan, see the install night, and log a fixture out with a picture instead of calling."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the system maps in place.

softwareAI.name: Fixture outage triage from a picture
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Clients send a night picture of the dark spot, and the assistant matches it to the system map and suggests whether it's a lamp, a wire or the timer."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7. Needs system maps and a set of past repair notes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Voice notes to lighting proposal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Talk through the demo, fixture by fixture, and it drafts the lighting proposal with counts, zones and the timer."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their proposal template and pricing. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Holiday tie-in offer sequence
softwareAI.pitchLine: "In early autumn, lighting clients get an offer to add holiday lighting on the same transformer and timer."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, only for companies that offer holiday lighting. Needs their offer and client list.

softwareAI.name: Night shot caption and page writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Upload the night shots and it drafts the project page and post, naming techniques and the neighbourhood, for you to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their notes and approval. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job costing per fixture installed
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See what each lighting job earns per fixture once fixtures, wire, transformer and tech hours are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs a season of supply invoices and tech hours.

softwareAI.name: Tech app with aiming and voltage checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Techs log voltage at the last fixture, aiming notes and a night picture per zone, so every install is documented."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, with two techs. Needs their install checklist.

softwareAI.name: Commercial facade bid sheet
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Facade and sign lighting bids come together on one sheet: fixture schedule, dark-sky notes, insurance and references."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, for firms chasing commercial lighting. Needs two past bids.

softwareAI.name: Applicant screener for lighting techs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants say whether they've done low-voltage lighting, can work evenings and have a licence, and you only call the fits."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Whenever they hire. Needs must-haves and pay range. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Night demo scheduler sold to lighting installers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every outdoor lighting installer fights the same sunset problem with demo bookings. One scheduler that follows the sun fixes it for all of them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Built once for one client; the sunset logic is identical everywhere.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Authorised installer locator for a fixture maker
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Homeowners who see your fixtures in a magazine can't find who installs them. A locator of trained installers with night galleries closes that gap."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Fixture makers fund dealer programs, and the lighting client proves you know the installer side.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give members a dark-gallery site with a night demo scheduler and technique pages as part of their dues."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: A niche association with a clear member need; one deal reaches many lighting firms.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Agency licence for the night-gallery template
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies struggle to make lighting clients' dark photos look good on a light template. License the night-first build."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies get a specialised build without learning the niche.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The downtown business association or city
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Main-street businesses apply for the facade lighting grant, see approved installers and track the install in one place."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Downtown programs fund facade improvements; the lighting client knows the work.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The outdoor lighting franchise, per territory
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Franchise owners post the same corporate night shots everywhere. A local page per territory with their own lit homes and demo calendar sells better."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Territory-level owners have budgets and want local proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Model homes look best lit at dusk. A lighting upgrade page with dusk shots sells the package to buyers before closing."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders like option revenue, and the lighting client becomes the default installer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Campus and church lighting service contracts
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Campuses and churches need a simple way to report dark paths and book seasonal re-aiming. A service portal keeps one lighting firm on contract."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Institutions buy yearly and value a documented service record.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Monthly fixture and LED price note
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A short note each month on fixture, lamp and wire prices, built only from supplier invoices installers share with you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Small niche, real need, honest data.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Venues sell evening events. A site that shows the grounds lit at night books more of them, and your client lit the grounds."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Venues have marketing money and need night views of their grounds.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: An outdoor lighting company in another metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Lighting is a small trade, so each metro gets one site from me with the night gallery. Yours would be the only one in your market."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Exclusivity is a selling point in a small niche.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Fix lighting sites with washed-out galleries
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The lighting company with a poor site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "If your night shots look grey and muddy on your current site, I can move them onto a dark gallery that shows the glow."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The problem is visible in seconds, and the fix is already built.

upsellLadder.offer: Lighting site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The lighting site and the care plan sit on one contract, so new night shots go up with one text."

upsellLadder.offer: Review asks after install night and profile posts
upsellLadder.trigger: The first lighting install since launch switches on.
upsellLadder.line: "Their lights came on last night. Let's ask for the review while they're still out on the lawn looking."

upsellLadder.trigger: A standout install is finished, or the gallery is still mostly placeholders.
upsellLadder.line: "That house you just lit deserves a blue-hour shoot. It'll lead the night gallery for a year."

upsellLadder.offer: Night demo scheduler with sunset times
upsellLadder.trigger: Demo requests pile up as evenings get shorter, or a demo gets booked before dark.
upsellLadder.line: "That demo booked at six in summer was in daylight. The scheduler follows sunset so every lighting demo is in the dark."

upsellLadder.offer: Service plan renewal and night-check reminders
upsellLadder.trigger: A past client calls about lights that need re-aiming or a dark fixture.
upsellLadder.line: "That re-aim call is the service plan in disguise. Let's offer it to every lighting client you have."

upsellLadder.offer: Night lighting preview from a daytime picture
upsellLadder.trigger: Form data shows prospects hesitating before booking a paid demo.
upsellLadder.line: "People hesitate to book a night demo blind. A preview of their own house lit gets them to say yes."

upsellLadder.trigger: A service call takes too long because nobody remembers where the transformer or wire runs are.
upsellLadder.line: "That hour hunting for a buried wire is why every lighting job needs a system map."
